statements.quote: It's important that we continue to lead in this space, but not without taking into consideration the broader impacts on our community. That’s where guardrails come in — independent investigations, more transparency, and proposals like requiring a kill switch.
statements.context: Asked whether Washington needs to step in on AI and what guardrails she would support.
statements.reason: She supports AI guardrails including a kill switch but names no catastrophic or serious danger from AI itself; her stated concerns are community impacts and jobs.

grade_reason: Her one substantive 2026 remark on AI backs guardrails such as a kill switch and talks about community impacts and jobs, but does not acknowledge catastrophic risk.
notes: 7 web searches ran, none refused. The site-restricted search of deniseforcongress.org returned no pages from that site, so the campaign Priorities page (https://deniseforcongress.org/priorities/, read 2026-11-14, undated) was opened directly: it says "Push for more guardrails and regulation of artificial intelligence" to balance investment in new technologies against protecting American jobs; undated campaign copy, left out of statements. The Couric interview is a written Q&A dated 2026-09-28; the date is the publication date, and the interview itself may have been earlier. The page's text was read in full through a direct download, because the fetch tool truncated it. The kill-switch proposal hints at a loss-of-control concern but names no consequence, so it was labelled D with boundary; a reviewer may consider C. As a non-member she could not have co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act; no letter or other record found. Results about other Powells (Dina Powell, Jerome Powell) were ignored.
